proof.text: If the covering family is empty, then $Z$ is empty. Take $S'=S$, $h=\mathrm{id}_S$ and $Y=\varnothing$; all assertions are immediate from the definitions, with the empty isomorphism open. Henceforth the family is nonempty; empty members and empty intersections remain allowed.

source.place: Empty-cover case, checked directly from the statement.

proof.text: All $H_i$, their pairwise and triple intersections, and the inverse images of these intersections in $Y_i$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Indeed $Z\to S$ is finitely presented and $S$ is qcqs, hence $Z$ is qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](2); in a quasi-separated scheme intersections of quasi-compact opens are quasi-compact. Finiteness makes inverse images of these opens quasi-compact, by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](3), and quasi-separated. Restrictions of flat maps to opens are flat by the local-ring definition [def-weil-flat-morphism]. The restrictions remain locally finitely presented by the affine-neighbourhood definition [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]; part (1) of the permanence lemma makes them quasi-compact and quasi-separated over $S$, so they are finitely presented. These observations also apply after any base change by part (3) of that lemma and [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change].

source.place: Tags 03GI, 01KV, 01S7, 01TS, 01U9; restriction and base-change hypotheses for all later uses of 01ZM.

proof.text: There is a quasi-compact open $V\subseteq S$ containing $\eta$ on which every $q_i$ is an isomorphism. To see this, choose an affine neighbourhood $S_0$ of $\eta$. By [lem-weil-pbc-local-ring-spec-limit-affine-neighbourhoods], the directed system of affine neighbourhoods of $\eta$ contained in $S_0$, with affine transitions, has limit $\operatorname{Spec}k(S)$. Apply [thm-pd-spreading-out](2) to the inverse of $(q_i)_\eta$, with the finitely presented objects $H_i|_{S_0}$ and $Y_i|_{S_0}$. Apply its equality clause (3) to the two inverse identities. This gives an inverse to $q_i$ over some affine neighbourhood. Directedness and finiteness of the family give one affine $V$ for all $i$. Set $D_i=Y_i\times_S V$. Its inclusion in $Y_i$ is quasi-compact: $V\to S$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1), and this property survives base change by (3).

source.place: Limits Tag 01ZM (lemma-descend-finite-presentation), clauses (2),(3); the generic-point instance of the affine-neighbourhood limit.

proof.text: We will repeatedly use the following density verification. If $F\to T$ is flat and $T$ is integral, its generic fibre is schematically dense. Over an affine $\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq T$, any affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $F$ maps to the generic fibre by $B\to B\otimes_R\operatorname{Frac}R$. If a section maps to zero, some nonzero $r\in R$ annihilates it. Apply [lem-sc-flat-invertible-sections-torsion-free] with the invertible sheaf $\mathcal O$ on that affine chart: multiplication by $r$ is injective. The section is zero. This proves injectivity on a basis and hence on every open by the sheaf axiom. Consequently the inverse image of any open of $T$ containing the generic point is schematically dense too: a section zero on that open is zero on the generic fibre and thus zero. This applies to $Z$, every $Y_i$, their open restrictions, and their flat base changes over integral bases.

source.place: Generic density from flatness: affine localization and the torsion-free-sections argument used in Temkin Corollary 3.5.4.

proof.text: Let $\nu:N\to S$ be the normalization in $k(S)$. Construct it by [lem-weil-pbc-relative-normalization], applied to $\eta\to S$. This morphism is affine: the inverse image of any nonempty affine of the integral $S$ is $\operatorname{Spec}k(S)$. Thus the required qcqs hypotheses hold. The cited statement makes $N$ integral and $\nu$ integral, and identifies its algebra on $\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq S$ with the integral closure $\overline R\subseteq k(S)$. Apply [lem-sbc-integral-closure-finite-normal-product] with its product consisting of the single field $k(S)$. Every local ring of $N$ is an integrally closed domain, so $N$ is normal. On the generic fibre the integral closure of $k(S)$ in itself is $k(S)$, hence $N_\eta=\eta$. The scheme $N$ is qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](3) and [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](2).

source.place: Tags 035F (lemma-integral-closure), 035I (lemma-characterize-normalization), 035L (lemma-normal-normalization); Temkin Corollary 3.5.4, normalization of the base.

proof.text: Write $\mathcal A=\nu_*\mathcal O_N$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-relative-spec](1) it is quasi-coherent. It is integral by the affine descriptions above. Use part (1), the subalgebra clause, of [lem-weil-pbc-integral-algebra-directed-colimit-finite]: let $\mathcal A_\lambda\subseteq\mathcal A$ run over its finite quasi-coherent subalgebras. Put $T_\lambda=\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_S\mathcal A_\lambda$ using the relative-spectrum anti-equivalence. Each $T_\lambda\to S$ is finite; locally its algebra is a subring of $k(S)$ containing $R$, so $T_\lambda$ is integral and $(T_\lambda)_\eta=\eta$. Transitions are finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-permanence-over-separated], hence affine. Sections of the colimit on affines are those of $\mathcal A$ by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-algebra-colimit]. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-spec-colimit-limit], affine-locally on $S$, and [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition] give $N=\varprojlim_\lambda T_\lambda$: factor cones on the inverse images of affine opens of $S$ and glue the unique factorizations by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing]. Include $\mathcal O_S$ as the initial subalgebra. All $T_\lambda$ are qcqs by affineness and the permanence lemma of step 2. No finite presentation of $T_\lambda\to S$ is needed.

source.place: Properties Tag 0817 (lemma-integral-algebra-directed-colimit-finite)(1), Limits Tags 01YW and 01YX; the finite submodifications in Temkin Corollary 3.5.4.

proof.text: Fix $i,j$, put $H=(H_i\cap H_j)_N$, and $F_i=(q_i^{-1}(H_i\cap H_j))_N$, $F_j=(q_j^{-1}(H_i\cap H_j))_N$. Their maps to $H$ are finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence](a). Both are flat, finitely presented over the normal integral $N$ by step 2, and have reduced geometric fibres by [lem-trf-geometric-reduced-fibre-locus-base-change] and restriction to opens. Hence [lem-trf-geometrically-reduced-eta-normal] applies to $F_i$ and $F_j$: every finite generic modification of either is an isomorphism. Over $V_N=\nu^{-1}(V)$ their maps to $H$ are isomorphisms by step 3. Let $D=(F_i)_{V_N}\simeq(F_j)_{V_N}$, with graph $\gamma:D\to P:=F_i\times_H F_j$. This $D$ is quasi-compact by step 3 and $P$ is quasi-separated, since it is finite over the qcqs $H$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-composition] and finite base change. Thus $\gamma$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1). Form its scheme-theoretic image $G\hookrightarrow P$ by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-image-qc-kernel].

source.place: Temkin Proposition 3.5.2 and Corollary 3.5.4 (printed pp. 20–21), comparison via a common finite graph; Stacks Tag 01R8 (lemma-quasi-compact-scheme-theoretic-image).

proof.text: The projections $p_i:G\to F_i$, $p_j:G\to F_j$ are finite: the projections of $P$ are finite by finite base change, and $G\hookrightarrow P$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite]; use [lem-weil-pbc-finite-composition]. Each $F_a\to H$ is separated because finite morphisms are affine, by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](3). Apply [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-partial-section] to $D\hookrightarrow F_i$, $F_j\to H$ and $\gamma$, and then interchange $i,j$. Both projections are isomorphisms over $D$, and their inverse images of $D$ are the graph copy of $D$ in $G$. This open is schematically dense in $F_i,F_j$ by step 4. It is schematically dense in $G$ as well: on an affine $W\subseteq P$, the image lemma identifies the ideal with the kernel of $\mathcal O_P(W)\to\mathcal O_D(\gamma^{-1}W)$; the affine quotient description [def-weil-closed-immersion] therefore injects $\mathcal O_G(G\cap W)$ into these sections. These opens cover $G$. Since $V_N$ contains $\eta$, both $p_a$ are generic isomorphisms. They are proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper]. Thus they are finite $\eta$-modifications, and the eta-normality established in step 7 makes both isomorphisms. Set $\phi_{ij}=p_jp_i^{-1}$ over $H$.

source.place: Tag 0CNG (lemma-scheme-theoretic-image-of-partial-section), Tag 01R8, Tag 035C; Temkin Corollary 3.5.4, explicit comparison of the two eta-normal sources.

proof.text: The overlap map is unique, and the same uniqueness holds after any integral base change under consideration. Indeed work over an affine $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq H$ lying above an affine $\operatorname{Spec}R$ of the base. Both models are affine there since finite. Two maps over $H$ yield homomorphisms from the target model's coordinate ring to the source model's ring $B$. Their generic restrictions agree, since each given finite map is a generic isomorphism. The map $B\to B\otimes_R\operatorname{Frac}R$ is injective by [lem-sc-flat-invertible-sections-torsion-free], as in step 4. The homomorphisms therefore agree on every element. The affine comparisons cover the models, so [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] makes the maps equal. This also proves that $\phi_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$, $\phi_{ji}=\phi_{ij}^{-1}$ and $\phi_{ik}=\phi_{jk}\phi_{ij}$ on triple overlaps.

source.place: Uniqueness and cocycle verification in Temkin Corollary 3.5.4 and Theorem 3.5.5, Step 1; affine torsion-free verification.

proof.text: Descend the finitely many $\phi_{ij}$ and their inverses from $N=\varprojlim T_\lambda$ using [thm-pd-spreading-out](2). All models on overlaps are finitely presented over $S$ by step 2, and the $T_\lambda$ are qcqs with affine transitions by step 6. Apply the equality clause (3) to both inverse identities and to $q_j\phi_{ij}=q_i$; here the comparison target $(H_i\cap H_j)_{T_\lambda}$ is finitely presented too. Choose a common later index for the finite list of maps and equalities. Put $S'=T_\lambda$. Its morphism $h:S'\to S$ is finite and proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper], and has generic fibre $\eta$. Its image is closed by properness and contains the generic point, hence equals $S$; thus it is surjective. The scheme $S'$ is integral by step 6. Uniqueness in step 9, using flatness over this integral $S'$, gives the cocycle for the descended overlap maps. It also forces their restrictions over $V'=h^{-1}(V)$ to be the identifications supplied by the isomorphisms $q_i|_{V'}$.

source.place: Temkin Corollary 3.5.4, descent from normalization to a finite submodification; Limits Tag 01ZM (lemma-descend-finite-presentation)(2),(3).

proof.text: On $F_i=Y_i\times_S S'$ take the overlap open $F_{ij}=q_i^{-1}((H_i\cap H_j)_{S'})$. The descended maps are over the base overlap, so $\phi_{ij}^{-1}(F_{ji}\cap F_{jk})=F_{ij}\cap F_{ik}$: both sides are precisely the inverse image of $(H_i\cap H_j\cap H_k)_{S'}$. Together with the cocycle this is the full hypothesis of [lem-weil-pbc-glue-schemes]. It gives a scheme $Y$ covered by the $F_i$. The maps $q_i:F_i\to Z_{S'}$ agree on overlaps, so [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] glues them to $q:Y\to Z_{S'}$. In fact $q^{-1}((H_i)_{S'})=F_i$: any representative in an $F_j$ whose image lies in $(H_i)_{S'}$ lies in the prescribed overlap, where it is identified with its representative in $F_i$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-local-on-target] proves $q$ finite. The generic restrictions are the given identities, so $q_\eta$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Temkin Theorem 3.5.5, Step 1 (printed p. 22); Schemes Tags 01JB (lemma-glue), 01JC (lemma-glue-schemes), Morphisms Tag 01WI (finiteness local on target).

proof.text: Each chart $F_i\to S'$ is flat and finitely presented by step 2. Its geometric fibres are reduced by [lem-trf-geometric-reduced-fibre-locus-base-change]. Since the $F_i$ are open in $Y$, flatness of $Y\to S'$ follows from [def-weil-flat-morphism] on local rings, and local finite presentation follows from [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] on affine neighbourhoods. The scheme $Z_{S'}$ is qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. The finite map $q$ is affine, hence qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](3); consequently $Y$ is qcqs by part (2) of the first lemma, and its map to the qcqs $S'$ is qcqs by part (1). It is therefore finitely presented. On each geometric fibre the $F_i$ remain an open covering, so [lem-trf-reduced-scheme-open-cover] gives reducedness of that fibre.

source.place: Flatness and finite presentation local on the source; Tags 01TS and 0576 (lemma-base-change-fibres-geometrically-reduced), reducedness local on an open covering.

proof.text: Finally put $U=Z_{S'}\times_{S'}V'$, viewed as an open in $Z_{S'}$. Step 10 shows that the restrictions of $q_i$ over $V'$ glue by their identity identifications; hence $q^{-1}(U)\to U$ is an isomorphism, by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] applied to their local inverses. Both $Z_{S'}\to S'$ and $Y\to S'$ are flat, the first by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change] and the second by step 12. As $V'$ contains the generic point of the integral $S'$, step 4, using [lem-sc-flat-invertible-sections-torsion-free], proves injectivity of restriction of sections to $U$ and to $q^{-1}(U)$ on every open. This is exactly schematic density on both sides [def-trf-schematically-dense-open].

source.place: Temkin §1.2 definition of modification and Theorem 3.5.5, Step 1; explicit target- and source-side schematic-density verification.

title: Finite-base reconciliation of local reduced generic modifications
statement: Let $S$ be an integral quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme], with generic point $\eta$ [def-sc-generic-point]. Quasi-compact quasi-separated means that there is a finite affine open cover with quasi-compact pairwise intersections. Let $Z\to S$ be flat and finitely presented [def-weil-flat-morphism] [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Let $H_1,\ldots,H_n$ be a finite cover of $Z$ by quasi-compact open subschemes [def-weil-open-immersion]. For each $i$, let $q_i:Y_i\to H_i$ be finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], inducing the given identification $(Y_i)_\eta\simeq(H_i)_\eta$, and suppose $Y_i\to S$ is flat and finitely presented and every geometric fibre is reduced [def-weil-geometric-fibre] [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. Then there exist an integral scheme $S'$ and a finite proper surjective morphism $h:S'\to S$ [def-weil-proper-morphism] [def-weil-surjective-morphism], with generic fibre $\eta$, such that the pullbacks of the $q_i$ agree by unique isomorphisms on every overlap $H_i\cap H_j$ after base change to $S'$. These isomorphisms are over the pulled-back overlaps and induce the given identity on generic fibres. They satisfy the cocycle condition and the pulled-back $Y_i$ glue to a scheme $Y$ and a finite morphism $q:Y\to Z\times_S S'$ [def-pc-base-change]. This $q$ is an isomorphism on the generic fibre and over an open $U\subseteq Z\times_S S'$ whose inclusion and inverse-image inclusion are schematically dense [def-trf-schematically-dense-open]. The morphism $Y\to S'$ is flat and finitely presented with reduced geometric fibres. No normality or finite-type-over-a-field or Noetherian assumption on $S$ is made.
